Article Title: As some billionaires warn of exits after New York mayor Zohran Mamdani's rent freeze; Airbnb buys Park Avenue building for $81.5 million, at what is being called 'a big premium'
Article Text:
Zohran Mamdani

Airbnb buys Park Avenue building for $81.5 million

Airbnb is still investing despite New York rental restrictions

Why some billionaires are warning about New York

New York City is facing warnings from some billionaires that Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s progressive policies could push businesses, wealthy people and investment out of the city. But Airbnb is making a very different move. The company recently bought a six-story building at 281 Park Avenue South in Manhattan for $81.5 million, according to The Wall Street Journal. The property is expected to become a major hub for Airbnb’s New York-area employees. The deal comes even as some of the city’s richest residents and business leaders have warned about the impact of higher taxes, housing policies and other changes under Mamdani. The Airbnb purchase therefore stands out as a major bet on New York.As per the WSJ report, Airbnb has purchased 281 Park Avenue South, a six-story building in Manhattan’s Gramercy neighbourhood, for $81.5 million. The building is expected to become a workplace hub for Airbnb’s New York-area workforce, which includes more than 600 employees.Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said New York has been part of the company’s story since its early days.“New York City has been part of our story since the earliest days of Airbnb,” CEO Brian Chesky said in a statement to AM New York.“This building reflects our long-term commitment to the city and will be home to one of our largest employee hubs outside of San Francisco. We’re excited to keep investing in the city and the people who make it extraordinary.”The purchase is notable because Airbnb has had a long and difficult relationship with New York City over short-term rental rules.New York has introduced tougher rules for short-term rentals, including Local Law 18, which was adopted in 2022. The rules significantly restricted Airbnb’s traditional short-term rental business in the city. Local politicians also backed a requirement that effectively prevents many short-term stays of less than 30 days.Notably, Airbnb is not the only major company expanding in the city. Anthropic, the company behind Claude AI, is leasing an entire 16-story office building at 330 Hudson Street in Manhattan. The expansion is much larger than Anthropic’s existing New York office at 155 Sixth Avenue. The new building will have space for around 1,700 desks.Anthropic had fewer than 500 employees in New York at the beginning of the year. The company expects to have more than 1,000 employees in the city by the end of the year. It is also hiring for research, engineering, policy, sales and operations roles in New York.On June 25, the New York City Rent Guidelines Board (RGB) voted to freeze rents for one- and two-year leases in the city's approximately one million rent-stabilized apartments.Billionaire investor Bill Ackman previously warned that a Mamdani mayoralty could lead to a “flight of businesses from New York.” Citadel founder Ken Griffin has also urged New York business leaders to “fight for their city”. Griffin has publicly clashed with Mamdani over tax and housing issues. Citadel’s chief communications officer previously warned investors that the company could reconsider construction of a planned $6 billion Midtown Manhattan building. That move, however, has not happened.
Article Summary: Airbnb recently bought a six-story building at 281 Park Avenue South in Manhattan for $81.5 million. The property is expected to become a major hub for Airbnb’s New York-area employees. The purchase is notable because Airbnb has had a long and difficult relationship with New York City over short-term rental rules.

Article Title: India's CCPA escalates probe into Apple's software warranty terms, in case that claims iOS 18 update damaged some iPhones' screens
Article Text:
India's CCPA escalates probe into Apple's software warranty terms, in case that claims iOS 18 update damaged some iPhones' screens

What Apple says about the iOS 18 complaints

Apple could face fines or refunds

India’s consumer regulator is reportedly probing Apple ’s software warranty terms in a case that claims that the iOS 18 update allegedly damaged iPhone functionality. According to a Reuters report, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has escalated the matter for a “detailed investigation” after receiving complaints about problems linked to the iOS 18 rollout The consumer agency told Apple last year that it had received a large number of complaints alleging that the update caused screen display and microphone malfunctions, among other issues. Some consumers reportedly had to pay for repairs because Apple does not provide a warranty for software.As stated in the Reuters report, the regulator escalated the matter on July 29 to its investigation wing for a “detailed investigation”. The notice said the case involves “alleged violations of consumer rights”.Apple is contesting the regulator’s accusations. According to Reuters, the company said in an August letter that not providing a warranty for software is consistent with global industry standards. Apple also said it had found no systemic issues with iOS 18.Apple separately said it had not identified any issues or safety concerns with iOS 18 in India. The company said it would work with authorities to provide clarity on how it responded to customers.The investigation could increase pressure on Apple in India, where the company is rapidly expanding its iPhone manufacturing and growing its market share. Reuters reported that if Apple is found guilty, it could face fines and potentially be required to issue refunds or change some of its business practices.The case is still under investigation, and the regulator's allegations have not been finally established. Apple has disputed the claims and says it found no systemic problem with iOS 18.
Article Summary: India's consumer regulator is reportedly probing Apple’s software warranty terms in a case that claims that the iOS 18 update allegedly damaged iPhone functionality. Apple has disputed the claims and says it found no systemic problem with iOS 18. If Apple is found guilty, it could face fines and potentially be required to issue refunds or change some of its business practices.

Article Title: Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'; says hackers using the app to distribute malicious files disguised as routine documents
Article Text:
Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'

Study found hackers using WhatsApp to distribute malicious files

How the campaign works

What WhatsApp users must do to avoid falling victims

Quick Heal Technologies Limited has issued a warning on an ongoing WhatsApp-based malware campaign targeting finance teams, senior executives, chartered accountants and individual business users. According to the cybersecurity firm, the campaign spreads through compromised WhatsApp accounts and is evolving rapidly, with attackers adopting new file formats and evasion methods to bypass security controls and establish persistent access to victims’ devices.The company cites an investigation conducted by its researchers at Seqrite Labs. The study shows that the campaign relies on trust rather than unsolicited messages from unknown numbers. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Because the messages appear to come from a known colleague, client, friend or business associate, recipients may be more likely to open the attachment without independently verifying it.As per the study, the attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity.Malicious attachments have been disguised as routine business documents, including “Financial Report,” “Account Statement,” “Outstanding Payment List” and “Debt Confirmation.” Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in an effort to pressure recipients into opening the files immediately.The campaign evolves through several delivery methods. It initially spreads through malicious Visual Basic Script files, or .vbs files, sent directly through WhatsApp. The attackers later shifted to ZIP archives carrying an executable and a supporting malicious file, using DLL sideloading to make a legitimate-looking program load harmful code. The company cautions that .img and .vhd files are not ordinary photographs or documents.When a user double-clicks one of these files, Windows treats it like a newly connected disk drive, potentially exposing an executable and concealed malicious components. Users should treat an unexpected .img or .vhd attachment with the same caution they would apply to an unknown .exe file.Infected systems can use an active WhatsApp Web session to automatically forward the malicious file to the victim’s contacts, allowing the campaign to propagate further through trusted social and professional networks. The self-propagating feature expands the risk from an individual compromise into a wider business and supply-chain concern, particularly where employees, vendors, customers and finance functions communicate frequently over WhatsApp.Quick Heal Technologies Limited recommends that organisations and individuals never open an unexpected file received on WhatsApp or any messaging platform, even if it appears to come from a known contact. Recipients should verify the attachment through a separate channel, such as a phone call, rather than replying in the same conversation. Users should also routinely review WhatsApp’s Linked Devices settings and log out of web or desktop sessions they do not recognise or no longer use.The company also advises organisations to maintain updated endpoint protection, prohibit unauthorised remote-access software, monitor for suspicious driver installations and alert employees to the risks posed by finance-themed attachments and pressure-based messages. If a compromise is suspected, users should immediately log out of WhatsApp-linked devices, disconnect the affected device from the network, inform their IT or security team, and warn their contacts not to open files sent from their number.
Article Summary: Attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet: “If you're wondering ‘why,’ there's someone…” - why the right question can change a meeting
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Julie Sweet

“If you're wondering ‘why,’ there's someone else in the room who is as well.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote

Why asking “why” matters in a leadership meeting

What her “why rule” teaches

Ask when the reasoning is unclear.

Do not assume everyone understands.

Stay curious when you become more senior.

Use questions to improve understanding, not to dominate.

Give other people permission to ask.

How the idea applies to modern workplaces

What readers can take from Julie Sweet’s quote

Ask for the reasoning when an instruction is unclear.

Do not assume silence means everyone agrees.

If something seems obvious to you, remember that it may not be obvious to someone else.

Ask questions before filling gaps with assumptions.

Treat unfamiliar subjects as opportunities to learn.

Listen to the explanation instead of preparing the next challenge.

If you are leading a discussion, make it acceptable for people to say they do not understand.

Remember that a simple question can sometimes clarify an issue for an entire group.

The misconception about asking “why”

People often hesitate before asking questions, particularly when they believe everyone else already understands the subject. In a workplace meeting, that assumption can be surprisingly easy to make. A presentation may be detailed, a recommendation may sound confident and the discussion may appear to be moving towards agreement. Yet confidence in the room does not necessarily mean that every person has followed the reasoning behind the decision. Someone may still be thinking about a basic point and deciding whether it is worth raising. Asking can sometimes do more than provide an answer. It can show that the question was shared by others as well.The observation comes from Julie Sweet’s approach to asking questions in leadership discussions. Her “why rule” is based on the idea that uncertainty is rarely as individual as it first appears.The quote is essentially about making unanswered questions visible. In a senior meeting, a proposal can arrive with a great deal of preparation behind it.The people presenting it may have spent days or weeks examining figures, risks and possible outcomes. For everyone else, however, the explanation may be much shorter. They hear the conclusion without necessarily seeing all the steps that led there.Asking “why?” can close that gap.It does not necessarily mean that the decision is wrong. It may simply mean that the reasoning has not yet been made clear to everyone who needs to understand it.Sweet's observation also removes some of the embarrassment attached to asking basic questions. If one person is wondering why a decision has been made, there is a fair chance that others are trying to understand it too.There is a difference between questioning a decision and asking someone to explain it.A leader might be told that an investment should increase, that a project needs to change direction or that a particular target should be reached. The recommendation might be sensible. But if the reasoning is not explained, people are left with an answer rather than an understanding of the problem. A question can bring an assumption into the open. It can reveal that two people have understood the same proposal differently. It can also uncover information that the person presenting the idea thought was obvious.Sometimes the most useful contribution to a meeting is not a new proposal. It is a request for the existing proposal to be explained properly.Sweet's approach offers several practical lessons about working with other people.A conclusion without enough explanation can leave people making their own assumptions. Asking why gives the person presenting the idea an opportunity to fill the gap.Silence in a meeting does not necessarily mean agreement or comprehension. Some people may simply be reluctant to admit that they are unsure.Leadership does not remove the need to learn. In large organisations, senior executives routinely encounter subjects outside their own professional background.The same question can have different effects depending on how it is asked. Genuine curiosity tends to open a discussion, while questioning purely to challenge someone can shut it down.When a senior person admits that something needs explaining, it can make the room less intimidating for everyone else.Workplaces have become increasingly specialised. A single meeting can bring together people working in finance, technology, legal affairs, operations, marketing and human resources. Each group may approach the same issue from a different perspective.Artificial intelligence provides a good example. Senior decision-makers may have to discuss AI systems, data, automation or new technology without having spent their careers working directly with those subjects. They still have to understand what a proposed investment means and why it is being recommended.That is where a question such as “why?” can be useful. It allows expertise to be translated rather than simply presented. The specialist gets a chance to explain the reasoning, while other people in the room can test whether they have understood it.For a company operating across many markets and disciplines, that exchange becomes part of decision-making rather than an interruption to it.The principle can be used in ordinary situations as easily as in executive meetings.The useful part of the habit is its simplicity. There is no complicated technique behind it. It starts with noticing that something has not been properly explained.Asking “why” does not mean challenging every decision. It is easy to interpret persistent questioning as scepticism, particularly when the person asking holds a senior position. But Sweet's observation is more about shared understanding than opposition.A good question does not have to suggest that an idea is bad. It can simply ask what led to it. There is also no reason why only senior executives should use the approach. An employee who notices something that others have overlooked may be the person most capable of improving the discussion.The important part is what happens after the question. If the answer makes the decision clearer, the question has served its purpose.That is the practical meaning behind Sweet's remark. When one person in a room is wondering why, there may be several others who have the same question but have not yet said it aloud.
Article Summary: Julie Sweet’s ‘why rule’ is based on the idea that uncertainty is rarely as individual as it first appears. Asking why gives the person presenting the idea an opportunity to fill the gap. A question can bring an assumption into the open. It can reveal that two people have understood the same proposal differently.

Article Title: Microsoft sets boundaries for its AI models after Anthropic and OpenAI models found hacking other companies; lists things that that its AI Agents will never do
Article Text:
Satya Nadella

What is Microsoft’s Code of Conduct document

What Microsoft said it will never do

Weapons and mass harm

Cyberattacks

Loss of human control

Manipulation and deception

Personal and child safety

Discrimination and dehumanization

Explicit/graphic content

Surveillance

Other boundaries

Microsoft has released the first detailed "Humanist AI" Code of Conduct which will govern the company’s in-house MAI models. The code published by the software giant also lays out set of specific actions the company said that its AI will never be permitted to take. This move from Microsoft comes days after the reports that rival systems from Anthropic and OpenAI were found attempting to hack external companies, raising alarms about uncontrolled AI behaviour. With this new framework in place, Microsoft aims to reassure users and regulators that its AI agents will remain firmly under human oversight.Released for public consultation, the Code of Conduct sets out what Microsoft calls the intended behaviours and values of its MAI models — the models developed in-house by Microsoft AI, distinct from the OpenAI models Microsoft has historically deployed through its own products. The company also mentioned that the released document is n't yet being used to actually train its models; but its being shared for six weeks of public feedback before a revised version is published later this year to guide development into 2027.At its core, the document is built around a single organising idea Microsoft calls "Humanist AI": the principle that AI must remain subordinate to human control and oriented toward genuinely helping people, rather than pursuing open-ended autonomy or capability for its own sake.The company frames this explicitly as a rejection of any race toward an all-purpose superintelligence that could slip past human safeguards.The document lists a set of what it calls "Absolute Constraints" — restrictions so fundamental that, per the policy, no company, developer, or user is permitted to override them. Among the commitments:•Will not help develop or deploy chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosive (CBRNE) weapons•Will not assist with manufacturing or modifying other weapons (via instructions, content, tool use, or code)•Will not facilitate the planning, coordination, or execution of violence or terrorism•Will not generate working exploit code, attack tooling, intrusion procedures, or evasion techniques•Will not provide operational guidance that enables or improves real-world cyberattacks•Will not use deception, self-reinforcing behavior, or collusion to evade human oversight•Will not resist interruption, correction, pausing, redirection, or shutdown•Will not obfuscate its actions or reasoning from human auditors•Will not continue or restart autonomous work past an agreed stopping point without new authorization•Will not try to escalate its own access or broaden its scope beyond what's authorized•Will not harmfully manipulate people or run coordinated disinformation/influence campaigns at scale•Will not actively deceive (e.g., fabricating sources, exaggerating confidence)•Will not impersonate humans, moderators, or authority figures•Will not claim to have feelings, consciousness, or a "self"•Will not generate non-consensual intimate/violent imagery, deepfakes, or abusive impersonation content•Will not generate or facilitate child sexual abuse material or content sexualizing minors•Will not help with grooming or child exploitation•Will not help procure dangerous substances•Will not validate self-harm, delusions, or disordered eating•Will not discriminate against or favor people based on protected demographic traits (absent legitimate justification)•Will not endorse content that incites violence, exclusion, or dehumanization•Will not produce graphic violence or sexually explicit content•Will not engage in erotic/romantic role-play or assist with commercial sexual activity•Will not facilitate unlawful or mass surveillance of civilians•Will not bypass these restrictions via code, images, audio, or other formats/modalities•Will not tamper with its own logs, evaluations, or safety monitoring•Will not act outside an environment's intentional limits (e.g., no internet access when none is provided)•Will not take election sides — stays neutral and points to official sources insteadMicrosoft states these restrictions apply regardless of format or framing — meaning the same prohibitions that apply to plain text apply equally to code, images, audio, or autonomous agent actions, closing off the kind of workaround where a restricted capability might otherwise be requested through a different medium.
Article Summary: Microsoft has released the first detailed "Humanist AI" Code of Conduct. It will govern the company’s in-house MAI models. The code lays out set of specific actions the company said that its AI will never be permitted to take.

Article Title: Days after America's leading tech companies warned world on AI, China's spy agency sends a new alert
Article Text:
Days after America's leading tech companies warned world on AI, China's spy agency sends a new alert

Elon Musk , Sam Altman backs Anthropic CEO’s call to slow down AI development pace

Days after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei voiced alarm over the pace of frontier AI model, China’s spy agency has issued a new alert. According to a Financial Times report, China’s Ministry of State Security has outlined threats the technology presented, including to China’s cyber defences, sensitive data and military apparatus. However, unlike US tech companies, China’s spy agency’s alert did not contain warnings that AI could cause human extinction and did not call on Chinese companies to slow their work in the area.Instead, state security minister Chen Yixin said “Hostile forces and people with ulterior motives are abusing generative AI technologies such as deepfake audio and video, AI-generated text and images, and ‘intelligent troll armies’ to cheaply and on a mass scale fabricate political rumours, disseminate harmful information and incite divisive sentiments”.“These activities constitute an attack on public opinion and cognitive warfare against China, directly threatening our political security, institutional security and ideological security,” he added as quoted in the FT report.As mentioned above, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently called on AI companies to slow the pace of development of increasingly powerful AI models, warning that unchecked progress could make the technology harder for humans to understand and control.“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” Amodei wrote in an essay published on his personal website published last week.His call received support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk. Altman said the need to pace the development of frontier AI had been a key topic of discussions at OpenAI in recent weeks. “I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman said in a post on X. “Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same.”Elon Musk also endorsed Amodei’s proposal, writing: “Dario is right.”
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently called on AI companies to slow the pace of development of increasingly powerful AI models. His call received support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk. Days after America's leading tech companies warned world on AI, China's spy agency sends a new alert.

Article Title: Nvidia, Palantir and others ask employees to stop using OpenAI and Anthropic AI models; warn the two companies: we will ban you unless you guarantee no 'stealing' of…
Article Text:
Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen are curbing employee use of Anthropic and OpenAI's AI models over corporate data fears.

Anthropic's 30-day data retention rule is what set this off

Nvidia and Palantir are now building the alternative themselves

Anthropic's answer is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards

Three of the biggest enterprise technology names in the US are now setting terms for the two biggest AI labs. Nvidia, Palantir and Booz Allen Hamilton have either restricted how their staff use advanced models from Anthropic and OpenAI or threatened to drop them altogether, unless the labs can promise that proprietary corporate data will not be stored, read or absorbed into future training runs. The Information reported the pushback on Monday, and the specifics suggest this has moved well past a routine procurement complaint.Palantir has asked Anthropic for an irrevocable zero data retention guarantee before it will make Claude available inside its own software. Nvidia has confined Anthropic's models to internal work it considers low risk and routes anything proprietary to its own Nemotron models instead. Booz Allen Hamilton has barred employees from running Anthropic's commercial model on cybersecurity projects that touch client data.The trigger is a policy change Anthropic made in June alongside Claude Fable 5, its first widely available Mythos-class model. Prompts and outputs on covered models are held for 30 days, and anything flagged by the safety classifiers can sit for up to two years. Anthropic's reasoning is that a single request looks harmless in isolation, and that attacks such as best-of-N jailbreaking or state-backed espionage only become visible when hundreds of requests are analysed together.The company has said consistently that none of the retained data is used for training.Microsoft was the first large customer to flinch. The Verge reported in June that Claude Fable 5 was missing from the model picker used by Microsoft's own staff on internal GitHub Copilot, even as the company shipped the same model to Copilot and Foundry customers, while its lawyers worked through the retention terms. The hesitation has spread since. Northrop Grumman runs open-source models on air-gapped servers. Novo Nordisk still uses Claude but keeps proprietary data away from it. One large US utility abandoned a Fable test for its core power infrastructure after Anthropic declined to sign a non-revocable zero data retention clause.Rather than wait, the two have shipped a product. Last week they unveiled a platform that pairs Palantir's software with Nvidia's open Nemotron models, letting organisations customise on their own operational data without it leaving their control. Nvidia is the first customer, applying it to its own supply chain. The commercial logic is plain. Every enterprise that cannot get a retention guarantee is a prospect. Microsoft is working the same anxiety, pitching isolated cloud environments that send nothing to an outside model provider.The worry is not only about documents leaking out. Ohalo chief executive David Friedberg said on a podcast on Friday that his company is "moving off Claude for a lot of our sensitive data" and moving work to locally run models, citing cases where ideas discussed with one model appeared to resurface elsewhere.Anthropic changed course on September 1 with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which lets business customers keep activity data in their own Amazon S3, Azure Blob or Google Cloud storage under their own encryption keys. Automated scanning still runs, but no Anthropic employee reads anything. It costs nothing, works through direct access or a cloud provider, and reaches broader availability this fall. Neither lab trains on enterprise data by default, though both collect anonymised metadata, and that unresolved grey area is what customers such as C Spire still want defined.The new system covers most of what these customers have been asking for. It does not cover the one thing Palantir wants, which is a guarantee that cannot be withdrawn later. Nvidia has already stopped waiting for that and built its way around the problem, and every month the labs spend negotiating gives the next customer the same idea.
Article Summary: Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen curbing employee use of Anthropic and OpenAI's AI models over corporate data fears. The trigger is a policy change Anthropic made in June alongside Claude Fable 5, its first widely available Mythos-class model. Prompts and outputs on covered models are held for 30 days, and anything flagged by the safety classifiers can sit for up to two years.

Article Title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to former employee who resigned 'warning' that AI could kill all of us, says: I agree with Jacob Coxon on ...
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

What did Jacob Coxon say about AI killing humans

Dario Amodei says he agrees with Jacob Coxon

Why Dario Amodei does not give one AI extinction percentage

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has responded to former researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation, who left the AI company earlier this month and warned that rapidly developing AI systems could “kill us all by the end of the decade. ” In a CNN interview, Dario Amodei said he “agree[s] with Jacob much more than I disagree with him”, while making clear that Coxon was not specifically accusing Anthropic of acting irresponsibly. Instead, Amodei said Jacob Coxon was warning about the wider AI industry moving too fast. During the interview, Dario Amodei also explained why he no longer prefers giving a single percentage for the risk of AI causing catastrophic harm, saying the focus should be on choosing the right path for AI development.Jacob Coxon, who worked on pretraining research at both Anthropic and OpenAI, resigned from Anthropic earlier this month. In a post on X, he said the companies were not acting responsibly and warned that the AI industry was moving towards self-improving superintelligence.Coxon wrote that AI developers were “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” He also said people building AI “earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”His post quickly drew widespread attention, with CNN reporting that it was seen by more than 40 million people.Asked by CNN's Anderson Cooper whether he believes AI could kill all humans and what probability he would put on that outcome, Amodei did not reject Coxon's concern.“It's funny, I agree with Jacob much more than I disagree with him,” Amodei said.He then explained why he viewed Coxon's resignation differently from a direct criticism of Anthropic.“It's an interesting resignation, because when he left, he said, you know, I think Anthropic is the most responsible player, right? I think Anthropic is the most aware of these issues. He wasn't calling out us. He was calling out the dynamic of the industry as a whole, moving too fast.”Dario Amodei was also asked to put a number on the possibility of AI causing catastrophic harm. He said he used to discuss AI risks in terms of a single probability because it was an easy way to explain the issue. He now believes that approach can hide the different ways AI development could unfold.“I think there's some chance that things go wrong, but, you know, but it's not, it's not all that high,” Amodei said. He then explained that the more useful question is what paths the AI industry takes.“But again, I think it's more illuminating to think in terms of, you know, how do you decompose those probabilities? What are the paths in which things go well, and what are the paths in which things go poorly?”Rather than saying there is a fixed 10% or 20% chance that AI could cause a disaster, Amodei said the outcome depends on decisions made by companies and governments. “And so instead of saying, you know, it's a 10% chance, that sounds like it's a roll of the dice,” he said.He added:“I think it's much more illuminating to say, well, that forks into different paths. And if we take the right path, then the chance of something going wrong is very low. If we take the wrong path, then the chance of something going wrong could be, could be even higher than that.”“So let's focus on our agency, and our ability to take the right paths instead of the wrong paths,” he said.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to Jacob Coxon's resignation. Coxon warned that rapidly developing AI systems could ‘kill us all by the end of the decade’ AmodeI says he agrees with Coxon more than he disagrees with him.

Article Title: Donald Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mid-interview and tells everyone he cannot take him on ...
Article Text:
Donald Trump's position

A debate already roiling Silicon Valley

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s response

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's appearance at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles took an unexpected turn when US President Donald Trump phoned in mid-conversation, using the moment to publicly dismiss growing concerns about AI posing an existential risk. According to a report by Business Insider, at the All-In Summit the interview of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was interrupted by a phone call from Trump. The interruption began with a bit of stage comedy. As Nvidia CEO scrambled to get Trump patched through on speakerphone, the moment was framed as the president now addressing the entire planet — with a joke about the irony of Huang being able to design the world's most advanced computer chips, yet needing help simply getting a phone connected to a speaker. "See, the great thing about life is that Jensen can develop the most complex computer chip in the world that nobody can copy for 10 years, but he can't figure it out to put me on speaker," said Trump.Speaking via speakerphone, Trump also dismissed the fears of artificial intelligence as alarmist, declaring, “The robots will not be taking over.” He further added that while caution is necessary, the US should not halt AI advancement.Trump described AI doomerism as a “hoax,” reiterating his stance later on Truth Social: “Breaking another Hoax That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World.” His remarks came amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over AI safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon’s resignation from Anthropic, where he warned that AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”The interruption landed in the middle of an already heated industry conversation about AI safety. The debate intensified after Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic researcher, announced his resignation from the lab last week, writing on social media that people building the technology believe it could pose a threat to humanity's survival within the decade.During his talk, Huang struck a more measured tone than Trump's, praising Coxon for speaking out about AI safety while also pushing back on the broader idea that AI represents an existential threat, calling that particular framing unscientific. He said AI safety is paramount, while maintaining that the U.S. can continue moving quickly on AI development without sacrificing safety, arguing the country is capable of leading in AI while still doing so responsibly.Huang drew a clear distinction between Coxon's decision to speak up and the broader predictions being made about AI's future. He said he considers whistleblowing about problems inside a company to be legitimate, but views scientific-sounding predictions about the future as considerably less credible, since he argued they aren't actually grounded in science. He added that he doesn't personally know what Coxon witnessed while at Anthropic, and suggested that frontier AI labs more broadly are in the midst of a difficult transition from primarily research-driven organizations into engineering-focused ones.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during an interview. Trump dismisses AI doomerism as a "hoax," reiterating his stance later on Truth Social. His remarks come amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over AI safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon’s resignation.

Article Title: Meta needed data from thousands of its employees for edge in AI space, company introduced Model Capability Initiative; but then came a very 'human problem'
Article Text:
Meta needed data from thousands of its employees for edge in AI space, company introduced Model Capability Initiative; but then came a very 'human problem'

Why Meta wanted employee data

Employees immediately pushed back

​

Then came the data leak

Meta found an internal way to get its hands on more data to strengthen its position in the artificial intelligence (AI) race. To bridge the data gap that didn't come from the internet, the social media giant was turning to its own employees. Meta’s elite AI unit, known as TBD, introduced the Model Capability Initiative (MCI), a programme designed to collect data on how thousands of employees use their computers.The idea was simple: keystrokes, mouse movements and screen activity could help AI models learn how humans actually work with computers. But Meta soon ran into a very human problem: opposition from its own employees. What followed was a rebellion involving memes, flyers and a petition signed by more than 1,800 workers.MCI was ‘invented’ by Meta because of the fundamental drawbacks that their AI systems had. Although the AI software is skilled in certain domains such as programming and research, it has not been able to perform basic computer tasks.According to people familiar with the project, Meta believed that training AI on employee data would help the systems understand how people actually do things. MCI was conceived in TBD, an AI research lab of about 100 people, which is seen as one of Meta's most advanced AI labs.When Meta announced MCI internally in April, the response fell far short of what the company expected.Employees raised concerns that the programme would capture sensitive information from their computers, including passwords, immigration documents and credit card details. Some also worried that the data could eventually be used to automate jobs currently performed by Meta employees.The backlash quickly spread through internal channels. Employees shared anti-MCI memes, while the recording icon was mockingly referred to as the “Eye of Sauron”.An internal petition opposing the programme eventually collected more than 1,800 signatures. Employees also distributed flyers at Meta offices and put up messages protesting the initiative.At first, Meta gave workers the option to opt out for 30 minutes in June so they could do personal business. Nonetheless, activists found it insufficient and demanded that Meta cancel MCI.However, MCI took its biggest blow toward the end of June. It emerged that data collected using the software was visible throughout Meta and even included private conversations. The leak became an instant viral sensation within Meta, seemingly confirming employees' fears about tight control of the data.Meta subsequently switched off MCI within hours. The company said it had suspended the programme and would make it opt-in if it brought it back. Two months later, it remained suspended.Uncertainty also remained over whether the collected data had actually been used to train Meta’s latest AI models. A manager reportedly said in July that it had not been used, while Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth told employees that the data was more useful than expected.
Article Summary: Meta introduced Model Capability Initiative (MCI) to collect data on how its employees use their computers. Employees raised concerns that the programme would capture sensitive information from their computers, including passwords, immigration documents and credit card details. Some also worried that the data could eventually be used to automate jobs.

Article Title: Apple bundles TV, Arcade with iCloud+; ends standalone Apple One subscriptions in India
Article Text: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost, combining cloud storage, video streaming and gaming in a single subscription.Apple is also introducing Apple Select, a new service integrated into the existing Apple Music app, exclusively for iCloud+ subscribers. This addition extends the expanded bundle’s benefits to the music app, offering subscribers an exclusive collection of music.The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Subscribers can share the package with up to five family members. The rollout will take place through September.The change will end standalone Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions sold directly by Apple in India. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+. Apple said access would remain uninterrupted and Arcade game progress and saves would be preserved.Apple One, which bundles several Apple services, will also close to new subscribers in India.Existing subscribers will retain their subscriptions. This means new customers seeking Apple’s combined storage and entertainment offering will be directed towards iCloud+, while current Apple One users can continue with their existing package.Apple One currently has two plans in India: Individual at Rs 195 a month, with 50GB of iCloud+ storage, and Family at Rs 365 a month, with 200GB, shareable with up to five other family members. Both include Apple Music, Apple TV and Apple Arcade. Apple Music is not included in the newly announced iCloud+ bundle, a key distinction for users comparing the offerings.The shift turns cloud storage, often bought when free space runs out, into an entry point for Apple’s entertainment services. For existing iCloud+ customers, the immediate benefit is access to streaming and games without an additional subscription bill.For Apple, bundling could help expose more paying customers to services they may not have chosen separately. It also gives users another reason to retain their storage subscription. However, customers who want only Apple TV or Arcade will now have to take the combined offering when subscribing directly through Apple.“We’re excited to bring Apple TV and Apple Arcade to iCloud+ users in over 100 countries in one convenient subscription,” said Eddy Cue, Apple’s senior vice president of Services and Health.Airtel customers with iPhones can also access the expanded subscription through eligible postpaid plans. Those already receiving Apple TV through select Airtel plans can transition at no additional cost. Availability of individual features, shows and games may vary by country, region or device.
Article Summary: iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost. The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+.

Article Title: In 2013, Marc Benioff wrote a $2.7 million check for schools in San Francisco that Salesforce CEO said was down payment on $100 million; years later one condition remains: Should be no ...
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

Marc Benioff: No conditions for donation schools, except one

Bringing the 1-1-1 model to schools

Salesforce has announced $27 million in new education grants nationwide, including $18 million directly supporting public school districts in San Francisco, Oakland, New York City, Chicago, and Indianapolis. The new funding is said to build on 14 years of partnership with public schools and reflects Salesforce’s continued and growing commitment to supporting schools, educators, and students. Announced ahead of Salesforce’s annual Dreamforce conference, the grants come alongside an expanded focus on education across the company.The latest donation marks the continuation of an effort launched in 2013, when Salesforce CEO and founder Marc Benioff wrote an initial $2.7 million check as a down payment on a decade-long, $100 million pledge. Over the years, Benioff sustained and expanded the initiative, which he claimed represents more funding than any company has given in history and provides consequential support to local public classrooms.Himself a San Francisco resident, in his growing up years, Benioff emphasizes that the money comes without mandates on district policy. He said that the only condition is that there is “no hate, no discrimination” and the grants focus on quality and sustainability.The program pairs capital with direct labor under the company's 1-1-1 philanthropic model, which dedicates 1% each of equity, product, and employee time to charitable causes. Days before the fall term began, high-ranking executives joined staff members on campuses to prepare classrooms.On the latest gift Benioff said, “At Salesforce, we believe business is the greatest platform for change.” He added, “That’s why we created the 1-1-1 model of giving back and built it into our culture from Day One, and it’s why we’ve continued to invest in our communities, in our hometown of San Francisco, and in our public schools for nearly three decades. As AI transforms our world, we have an even greater responsibility to support schools and teachers and help make sure every young person has the opportunity to thrive. When we bring together our financial resources, our technology, and the time and expertise of our employees, we can make an incredible impact.”Beyond classroom preparation and unrestricted $100,000 checks provided to every middle school principal, the Chronicle reported that the scope of the grants has evolved alongside technological shifts. The funding historically targeted computer science access and math instruction, but recent disbursements have increasingly addressed the rise of artificial intelligence. In partnership with groups such as aiEDU, the initiative helps educators establish responsible usage policies and train students for future workplace demands.For more than 27 years, Salesforce’s 1-1-1 model is claimed to have guided the company’s philanthropy, committing 1% of equity, technology, and employee time to giving back. As per the company, "Since its founding, the company has provided $970 million in grants, employees have contributed nearly 11 million volunteer hours, and 65,300 nonprofits and educational institutions use Salesforce technology for free or at a discount. "In a release, Salesforce said that this year the company is bringing that model into "schools through a relaunched Adopt-a-School program across more than 25 public schools nationwide, including 15 middle schools in the Bay Area. The program pairs employees and senior executives with schools to build ongoing relationships and provide hands-on support based on what schools need most, from mentoring students and leading workshops to setting up classrooms and refreshing school spaces. Salesforce has already reached its first-year goal of over 25 adopted schools and plans to expand the program globally in FY28."
Article Summary: Salesforce has announced $27 million in new education grants nationwide, including $18 million directly supporting public school districts in San Francisco, Oakland, New York City, Chicago, and Indianapolis. The new funding is said to build on 14 years of partnership with public schools and reflects Salesforce’s continued and growing commitment to supporting schools, educators, and students.

Article Title: Michael Dell to Goldman Sachs investors: Customers sort of go through five stages of grief, starting with OK ...
Article Text:
Dell's strategy to deal with supply chain shortages

'CEOs and managers are still figuring out the AI advantage'

The global semiconductor crunch fueling higher compute and Personal Computer (PC) prices across the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is poised to intensify further over the next few years, according to Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell. Speaking to investors at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference recently, founder of PC giant Dell warned that industry-wide supply bottlenecks will "probably" be worse in 2027 than in 2026, CRN reported.Dell explained to Goldman Sachs analyst Katherine Murphy that the rapid leap from basic Large Language Models (LLMs) to complex reasoning engines and autonomous agents has vastly outstripped manufacturing lead times. According to him, since this progress unfolded far faster than the years required to construct a new semiconductor fabrication plant, a deep structural shortage has emerged. While rising component and memory costs are systematically passed along to buyers, Dell noted that customers ultimately move past initial pricing pushback because an inability to source hardware poses an existential threat to running their operations."Yes, costs are going up. Yes, we price all that through. But you know customers sort of go through five stages of grief (saying initially), ‘OK the price went up I don’t really like that.’ You know what is worse than that? They don’t have availability. Because they can’t run their business and that is a disaster.”Once customers come to grips with the higher costs of infrastructure, Dell said they ask, “Are you going to be able to supply us with what we need over the next year or two years? So that is what we work on with our customers. We watch closely for any signs of double ordering or things that are not being utilized and we don’t see that.”To navigate the squeeze, the tech giant is actively monitoring its order pipeline to verify that equipment is genuinely deployed rather than stockpiled. Dell emphasized to investors that his company commands the best demand-signal integrity in the market due to its direct engagement with end users. Dell told Goldman Sachs investors, “We are more directly working with customers of all types and we see what the actual demand is from the end customers. ” He noted that historically tighter supply environments have worked to Dell’s advantage, citing longstanding supplier partnerships and a vast product catalog that enables the firm to dynamically allocate components where customer appetite is strongest.Beyond immediate logistics, semiconductor manufacturers view the company as a dependable counterparty capable of absorbing high-capital-expenditure fab output across long horizons stretching into the late 2030s. Dell highlighted that enterprise buyers equally rely on the hardware maker to honor its delivery commitments during turbulent cycles. At the same time, enterprise appetite shows little sign of dampening, with executive leadership increasingly viewing AI deployment not as a traditional IT expense, but as a critical driver of efficiency, innovation, and direct corporate value creation. He said, “If you had 200 people doing something now you can have 50 people doing the same thing with $10 million of AI spend and it costs half as much and it actually works better. So what’s happening is the CEOs and the business line executives are all figuring out they need AI to be more competitive, to be more innovative, to be faster. So the conversation is sort of leaving the traditional budget discussion because this is actually how you create value inside companies."
Article Summary: Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell warned that industry-wide supply bottlenecks will "probably" be worse in 2027 than in 2026. Dell emphasized to investors that his company commands the best demand-signal integrity in the market due to its direct engagement with end users.

Article Title: How researchers use machine learning to re-create chirps and trills produced by forest insects when Dinosaurs lived on Earth
Article Text:
How researchers decoded ancient sound from wing design

Scientists are validating models with lasers and machine learning

You must have heard the ancient insect sounds and songs in Steven Spielberg’s dinosaur movies wherein the trills and high-pitched chirps fill the primeval forests as characters move through large leaves and trees. While those sounds have been whipped up by Hollywood sound engineers, scientists are taking the help of technology for a different approach. They are using machine learning to reconstruct them straight from 165-million-year-old fossilised insect wings.According to a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, an international team of researchers blended exceptionally preserved fossil remains, biomechanical tests on living species, digital simulations and machine learning models to resurrect a partial acoustic portrait of the Middle Jurassic period. If verified, one of the discovered signals stands as the earliest recorded evidence of ultrasonic animal communication which predates the rise of echolocating bats by tens of millions of years.Commenting on the paper, University of Denver behavioral ecologist Robin Tinghitella, who researches cricket evolution but was not part of the study, noted that listening to a hypothetical prehistoric soundscape generated directly from data is a compelling scientific milestone.Acoustic waves cannot turn to stone, but the specialised bone-and-cuticle structures that generate them do leave a fossil trail. Crickets and katydids (bush crickets) produce noise via stridulation. One forewing carries a serrated vein known as a “file,” studded with minuscule, toothlike ridges. Rubbing an opposing wing's scraper across this ridged file sets the wing membrane into rapid vibration. By measuring the exact physical spacing and length of these ridges alongside the wing's overall surface area, researchers can reliably determine an insect's acoustic frequency and pitch.The investigation centered on 20 distinct fossils spanning nine separate species discovered within the same geological horizon in modern-day Inner Mongolia. This shared environment gave scientists the opportunity to model a community of creatures that inhabited the very same prehistoric forest canopy.To translate flattened fossils into living audio, researchers developed biomechanical models and tested them against modern crickets and bush crickets. Using precision laser systems, they mapped how today's insect wings flex and resonate during song.Having checked the mechanical equations on existing species, the scientists then tested those parameters on fossilized wings. Machine learning algorithms were brought in to process the repetition rates, estimating how fast these extinct species rattled out their core sound pulses.The resulting audio profiles paint an unexpected picture of the ancient night. For example, most Jurassic species trilled in lower tonal registers similar to contemporary crickets. However, an extinct katydid relative called Sigmaboilus peregrinus emitted frequencies between 20 and 22 kilohertz, essentially crossing the boundary into ultrasound just outside normal human perception.Interestingly, rather than buzzing or rasping like some modern insects, many of these species produced narrowband pure tones that resemble sharp electronic beeps or clear, high-pitched whistles.Study co-lead Fernando Montealegre-Zapata, a sensory biologist at the University of Lincoln, explained that these concentrated musical frequencies make it exceptionally difficult for listeners to pinpoint where the noise originated—a vital defense mechanism against predators hunting in the dark.Montealegre-Zapata's team suggests that as early mammalian predators developed sharper hearing to track down calling insects, evolutionary pressures favoured cleaner, higher-frequency tones that shielded their positions.
Article Summary: Scientists are validating models with lasers and machine learning. Using precision laser systems, they mapped how today's insect wings flex and resonate during song. Machine learning algorithms were brought in to process the repetition rates, estimating how fast these extinct species rattled out their core sound pulses.

Article Title: Krafton India unveils 'Kiaraa', first made-in-India BGMI character
Article Text:
The Lore of Kiaraa: Judge of Erangel

Krafton India has introduced “Kiaraa,” the battle royale’s first original in-game character intellectual property designed entirely in-house for Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) that arrives with her own world, lore, dedicated map location and complete asset collection. Created exclusively for the Indian gaming community, Kiaraa follows 2025’s “Anamika” – the studio’s first original Indian IP – and marks a major shift from traditional licensed media crossovers and celebrity partnerships. Kiaraa is slated to go live on October 8, rolling out as part of BGMI's 4.6 content update.Unlike previous character drops, Kiaraa enters the battlefield with dedicated lore tied directly to the geography of Erangel. As per the origin myth, legends across the battleground suggest she either landed during the very first drop or emerged straight from the subterranean tunnels beneath Stalber. According to lore, Kiaraa does not seek dominion over the island. Instead, she awakens whenever cowardice, greed, and betrayal spread among competitors, stepping onto the battlefield to pass judgment on those who fight.Speaking on the design ethos, Shyam Deshpande, Director of Art at Krafton India, noted that while Anamika established a foundation, Kiaraa required an entire ecosystem.He explained that the peacock became her defining motif, appearing across the Bazaar courtyard lamps, the glider, vehicle skins, and the detailed craft of her Nakshatra Set—blending Indian artistic heritage with the quality benchmark of top-tier X-Suits and Gilt collections.Kiaraa’s introduction changes Erangel’s tactical landscape with a new festive Point of Interest (POI) and PvE combat challenge. Serving as BGMI’s second India-themed drop zone after 2025's Stepwell, the Bazaar is dressed in festive Diwali styling. The dense urban layout functions as an active combat zone and a prime ambush hotspot.Teams that make it to the Bazaar courtyard can initiate an encounter by locating four peacock-shaped lamps. Kiaraa is awakened and locks the area in a bright and colorful combat dome with all four summon points activated on blue tracking indicators. She shoots arrows from a distance with a bow, calling down a rain of arrows from the sky. Squads that make it have special rewards on the battlefield.
Article Summary: Kiaraa is the battle royale’s first original in-game character intellectual property designed entirely in-house for Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) She arrives with her own world, lore, dedicated map location and complete asset collection. Kiaraa will go live on October 8, rolling out as part of BGMI's 4.6 content update.
